name: Effective VC Radius
definition: For a family $\mathcal{H}\subset 2^\mathcal{X}$, we define the **effective VC radius** as the largest integer $k$ such that all subsets of size $k$ of the effective range of $\mathcal{H}$, i.e. $\bigcup \{h\Delta h': h,h'\in \mathcal{H}\}$ are shattered by $\mathcal{H}$.
graph_summary: The largest VC dimension obtainable after restricting to an effective trace.
comments: Not c-monotonic: $\mathcal H=\{000,001,010,100,110\}$ has effective VC radius $1$, while conditioning the last coordinate to $0$ gives the full two-dimensional cube, of effective VC radius $2$.

monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\{000,010,100,110\}$ is a two-cube (with a constant third coordinate), so its effective VC radius is 2. Adding $001$ activates the third coordinate, but the resulting class does not shatter the first-and-third-coordinate pair, so its effective VC radius falls to 1.

c_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: H={000,001,010,100,110} has effective VC radius 1; conditioning its last coordinate to 0 gives the full two-cube, of effective VC radius 2.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\mathcal H=\{000,001,010,100,110\}$ has effective VC radius 1, whereas projection to its first two coordinates is the full two-cube and has effective VC radius 2.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
